original_test_intent: Prove that an actual open circuit at the designated tray leak-sensor connector is diagnosed as a sensor fault and reported through the correct BMC channels, then restore the protection circuit safely.
original_method: Map and inspect the exact sensor-to-board connection, choose the approved power and coolant operating state, capture baseline evidence, have a qualified operator unplug that connector once, record the fault transition and management events, reseat it under the recovery procedure, and verify normal protection and connector condition.
manual_activity: Qualified hardware personnel identify, photograph, disconnect, inspect, and reseat the specified leak-sensor connector under an approved tray isolation and ESD procedure.
required_inputs: Tray, board, sensor, harness, and connector designators
Permitted power, coolant pressure/flow, pump, and valve state
Expected tray fault, BMC sensor/event identifiers, polarity, and latency
Reconnect, inspection, fault-clear, and recovery acceptance
safety_requirements: Verify energy and coolant state before touching the connector
Use ESD and connector-latch controls; never pull wires
Stop for liquid, heat, arcing, damage, unexpected actuator action, or wrong identity
Do not repeat after abnormal behavior
agent_execution_scope: Collect the approved mapping and procedure
Capture non-destructive authenticated management baselines if authorized
Correlate fault assertion and clearing with BMC events
Do not touch hardware, infer connector identity, simulate the open circuit, direct an unsafe power state, retry, or issue PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Define diagnostic and BMC acceptance matrix
Disposition anomalies and provide the formal verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It correctly states that software cannot create the required connector open, but does not specify how physical identity, safe isolation, fault assertion, or recovery will be proven.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: No command replaces the manual disconnect; use only authorized read-only sensor, Redfish, and SEL collection as corroborating evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Physical leak-sensor unplug, tray fault detection, correct BMC signals, no bundle, and 60/60-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: QUALIFIED MANUAL OPEN-CIRCUIT SENSOR FAULT TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a controlled connector-level stimulus with immutable before/asserted/recovered physical and BMC evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact hardware identity, safe state, expected diagnostic semantics, and connector restoration criteria.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A software-injected fault or preexisting SEL entry cannot prove wiring-open detection at the physical board input.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The wrong or energized connector can damage pins/electronics, disable leak protection, alter cooling controls, or create an unsafe liquid-cooled state.

project_override_considerations: Do not borrow the adjacent GB-NV-PVP connector map or treat a BMC sensor override as equivalent coverage. If the approved procedure requires powered operation to detect the open, the engineer must explicitly define safe access and coolant controls.
expected_evidence: Baseline connector photos and power/coolant/ESD state
Timestamped one-time disconnect and physical observation
Exact tray diagnostic plus complete BMC/Redfish/SEL assertion evidence
Reseat inspection, fault clear, restored protection/health, and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Preserves the actual connector-open stimulus and adds the missing identity, energy controls, diagnostic contract, evidence correlation, and safe restoration.
independent_technical_reasoning: This case tests electrical continuity supervision, not merely whether the BMC can display an alarm. The evidence must establish that the intended physical conductor changed from connected to open and that the tray diagnostic—not a coincident historical event—asserted within the accepted interval. Reconnect evidence is also functional coverage: the fault must clear without damaged pins, intermittent contact, or a disabled protection channel. Because both the stimulus and inspection require direct access, telemetry automation cannot change the MANUAL ONLY classification.
